doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dallas memories and the Denver years
title: No jazz instruction at Denver in the 1950s
summary: Faculty played jazz at night but not in class; Walton and friends did their own little arrangements, none of which entered his repertoire.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Was there a specific jazz instruction, uh, or …
Yeah, they played at night at nightclubs, but they didn't bring it into the classroom.
I initiated with uh me and a bunch of pals, you know, pals in the music department, little arrangements, then we had so much fun. But it was also curriculum.
So uh, no, it hadn't, this uh this kind of curriculum had not started yet and this is in the '50s now.
Now were there any … You said you initiated and you wrote some things. Are there any things that later became a part of your, of your original repertoire that have their origin in your time there?

Not one. No. Just a school issue, a school experiment at that time. I didn't uh, I didn't have any plans for it. I mean, you know, I didn't know how to, anything about how the business worked. I just … but I wanted to experience that on campus. So did they.
